# Consistency of OLS

## OLS in terms of sample averages

::: {.hidden}
\gdef\E#1{\mathrm{E}\left[#1\right]}
\gdef\Var#1{\mathrm{Var}\left(#1\right)}
\gdef\Cov#1{\mathrm{Cov}\left(#1\right)}
\gdef\rank#1{\operatorname{rank}\left(#1\right)}
:::

- Regression, $\{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\}$ iid:
  $$
  Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i, \qquad X_i \in \mathbb{R}^k
  $$

- OLS, $\rank{X} = k$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_n &= (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top Y \\
  &= \beta + \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## LLN for $\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i U_i$

- **Assume:**
  $$
  \E{X_i U_i} = 0, \qquad \E{U_i^2} < \infty, \qquad \E{X_{i,j}^2} < \infty, \quad j = 1, \ldots, k
  $$

- Cauchy-Schwarz: integrability for the weak LLN:
  $$
  \E{|X_{i,j} U_i|} \le \sqrt{\E{X_{i,j}^2}\, \E{U_i^2}} < \infty
  $$

- $X_1 U_1, \ldots, X_n U_n$: iid; weak LLN, element by element:
  $$
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \to_p \E{X_i U_i} = 0
  $$

## LLN for $\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top$

- Cauchy-Schwarz, element $(r, s)$:
  $$
  \E{|X_{i,r} X_{i,s}|} \le \sqrt{\E{X_{i,r}^2}\, \E{X_{i,s}^2}} < \infty
  $$

- **Assume:** $\E{X_i X_i^\top}$ p.d.

- Weak LLN and Slutsky for the inverse:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top &\to_p \E{X_i X_i^\top} \\
  \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} &\to_p \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Assumptions

- Assumptions for consistency:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\} \ \text{ iid} \\
  & Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i \\
  & \E{X_i U_i} = 0 \\
  & \E{U_i^2} < \infty \\
  & \E{X_{i,j}^2} < \infty, \quad j = 1, \ldots, k \\
  & \E{X_i X_i^\top} \ \text{ p.d. (no perfect multicollinearity)}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Weaker than $\E{U_i \mid X_i} = 0$:
  $$
  \E{X_i U_i} = 0 \quad \nRightarrow \quad \E{Y_i \mid X_i} = X_i^\top \beta \quad \text{(in general)}
  $$

## Consistency

- **Definition.** $\hat\beta_n$ consistent for $\beta$: $\hat\beta_n \to_p \beta$.

- **Theorem.** Under the assumptions for consistency:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_n &= \beta + \Big(\underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top}_{\to_p\, \E{X_i X_i^\top}}\Big)^{-1} \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i}_{\to_p\, 0} \\
  &\to_p \beta \qquad \text{(Slutsky)}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Asymptotic normality of OLS

## Assumptions I and II

- Approximate the distribution of $\hat\beta_n - \beta$: scale by $\sqrt{n}$.

- **Assumption I.**
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\} \ \text{ iid} \\
  & Y_i = X_i^\top \beta + U_i, \qquad \beta \in \mathbb{R}^k
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- **Assumption II.**
  $$
  Q = \E{X_i X_i^\top} \quad \text{p.d. and finite}
  $$

- Normalized OLS representation:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) = \underbrace{\Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1}}_{\to_p\, Q^{-1}}\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i
  $$

## Assumption III and the CLT

- **Assumption III.**
  $$
  \E{X_i U_i} = 0, \qquad \Omega = \Var{X_i U_i} \quad \text{finite and p.d.}
  $$

- Variance of $X_i U_i$, with $\E{X_i U_i} = 0$:
  $$
  \Omega = \Var{X_i U_i} = \E{X_i U_i (X_i U_i)^\top} = \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}
  $$

- $X_1 U_1, \ldots, X_n U_n$: iid; multivariate CLT:
  $$
  \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i \to_d N(0, \Omega)
  $$

## Limit of $\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta)$

- Cramér convergence theorem, without proof: $A_n \to_p A$, $A$ non-random, $Z_n \to_d Z$:
  $$
  A_n Z_n \to_d A Z
  $$

- Apply to the normalized representation; $Z \sim N(0, \Omega)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) &= \underbrace{\Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1}}_{\to_p\, Q^{-1}}\ \underbrace{\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i}_{\to_d\, Z} \\
  &\to_d Q^{-1} Z \sim N(0, Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}) \qquad (Q = Q^\top)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Asymptotic variance

- **Theorem.** Under Assumptions I to III:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \to_d N(0, V), \qquad V = \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) = Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}
  $$

- CDF form, for all $a \ne 0$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$:
  $$
  \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t\big) \to \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{a^\top V a}}\Big)
  $$

- $a = e_j$, element $j$:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j) \to_d N(0, [V]_{jj})
  $$

## Homoskedasticity

- Suppose:
  $$
  \E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2 \quad \text{(homoskedasticity)}
  $$

- Law of iterated expectations:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Omega &= \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top} \\
  &= \E{\E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \mid X_i}} \\
  &= \E{\underbrace{\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i}}_{=\,\sigma^2} X_i X_i^\top} \\
  &= \sigma^2 \E{X_i X_i^\top} \\
  &= \sigma^2 Q
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- The sandwich collapses:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\beta_n) &= Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} \\
  &= Q^{-1} (\sigma^2 Q) Q^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 Q^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Finite sample against large sample

- Normal errors, exact conditional distribution; $a \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & Y = X\beta + U, \qquad U \mid X \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n) \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \hat\beta_n \mid X \sim N\big(\beta,\ \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}\big) \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t \mid X\big) = \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 a^\top (X^\top X)^{-1} a}}\Big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Homoskedastic errors, large sample, $a \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \text{Assumptions I and II}, \quad \E{X_i U_i} = 0, \quad \E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2 > 0 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \mathrm{P}\big(a^\top \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \le t\big) \to \Phi\Big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 a^\top \big(\E{X_i X_i^\top}\big)^{-1} a}}\Big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Estimation of the asymptotic variance

## The estimator $\hat V_n$

- Unknown asymptotic variance:
  $$
  V = Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}, \qquad Q = \E{X_i X_i^\top}, \qquad \Omega = \E{U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}
  $$

- Sample averages and residuals in place of expectations and errors:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat V_n &= \hat Q_n^{-1} \hat\Omega_n \hat Q_n^{-1}, \\
  \hat Q_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top, \qquad \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p Q^{-1}, \\
  \hat\Omega_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Residual and error, fixed $i$; continuous mapping, without proof:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat U_i &= Y_i - X_i^\top \hat\beta_n = U_i + X_i^\top \underbrace{(\beta - \hat\beta_n)}_{\to_p\, 0} \\
  &\to_p U_i
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Can we use the LLN on $\hat\Omega_n$?

- **Definition.** Small $o_p$:
  $$
  Z_n = o_p(1) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad Z_n \to_p 0
  $$

- Fixed $i$: $\hat U_i = U_i + o_p^i(1)$:
  $$
  \hat\Omega_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i + o_p^i(1)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \overset{?}{=} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top + o_p(1)
  $$

- Fixed-$i$ convergence does not control an average over $n$ observations.

- Direct iid LLN unavailable: residuals share $\hat\beta_n$:
  $$
  \hat U_i = U_i - X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)
  $$

## Matrix norm

- Frobenius norm of a $k \times k$ matrix $A$:
  $$
  \|A\| = \sqrt{\sum_{r=1}^k \sum_{s=1}^k A_{rs}^2} = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(A^\top A)}
  $$

- Element by element $\Longleftrightarrow$ in norm; to show:
  $$
  \|\hat\Omega_n - \Omega\| \to_p 0
  $$

## Expansion of $\hat\Omega_n$

- Substitute $\hat U_i = U_i - X_i^\top(\hat\beta_n - \beta)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\Omega_n &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i - X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top + \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top \\
  &\qquad - 2\, \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) X_i X_i^\top
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- First term, weak LLN; $\Omega$ finite (Assumption III):
  $$
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top \to_p \Omega
  $$

- To show: the other two terms $\to_p 0$.

## Cauchy-Schwarz and $\|X_i X_i^\top\|$

- Cauchy-Schwarz:
  $$
  \big|X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big| \le \|X_i\|\, \|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|
  $$

- Frobenius norm, $\operatorname{tr}(AB) = \operatorname{tr}(BA)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \|X_i X_i^\top\| &= \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(X_i X_i^\top X_i X_i^\top)} \\
  &= \sqrt{(X_i^\top X_i)^2} = \|X_i\|^2
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Cross term $\to_p 0$

- **Assume:** $\E{U_i^4} < \infty$, $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$.

- Cauchy-Schwarz twice:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{|U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3} &\le \sqrt{\E{U_i^2 \|X_i\|^2}\, \E{\|X_i\|^4}} \\
  &\le \sqrt{\sqrt{\E{U_i^4}\, \E{\|X_i\|^4}} \cdot \E{\|X_i\|^4}} < \infty
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Triangle inequality, Cauchy-Schwarz, then weak LLN and consistency:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(U_i X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big) X_i X_i^\top\Big\| &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |U_i|\, \big|X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big|\, \|X_i X_i^\top\| \\
  &\le \Big(\underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3}_{\to_p\, \E{|U_i|\, \|X_i\|^3}}\Big) \underbrace{\|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|}_{\to_p\, 0} \\
  &\to_p 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Squared term $\to_p 0$

- Triangle inequality and Cauchy-Schwarz, then weak LLN and consistency:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Big\|\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big\| &\le \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(X_i^\top (\hat\beta_n - \beta)\big)^2\, \|X_i X_i^\top\| \\
  &\le \Big(\underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \|X_i\|^4}_{\to_p\, \E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty}\Big) \underbrace{\|\hat\beta_n - \beta\|^2}_{\to_p\, 0} \\
  &\to_p 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## $\hat\Omega_n \to_p \Omega$ and $\hat V_n \to_p V$

- Combine the three terms:
  $$
  \hat\Omega_n = \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top}_{\to_p\, \Omega} + o_p(1) \to_p \Omega
  $$

- **Theorem.** Assumptions I to III, $\E{U_i^4} < \infty$, $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$:
  $$
  \hat V_n = \hat Q_n^{-1} \hat\Omega_n \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} = V \qquad \text{(Slutsky)}
  $$

# Robust and usual standard errors

## Robust standard errors

- $\overset{a}{\sim}$: approximate distribution for large $n$:
  $$
  \hat\beta_{n,j} \overset{a}{\sim} N\Big(\beta_j,\ \frac{[V]_{jj}}{n}\Big)
  $$

- **Definition.** Robust (heteroskedasticity-consistent, White) standard error:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) &= \sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj} / n} \\
  &= \sqrt{\Big[(X^\top X)^{-1} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big) (X^\top X)^{-1}\Big]_{jj}}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Recall: $\E{U \mid X} = 0$, $\Var{U \mid X} = \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2, \ldots, \sigma_n^2)$:
  $$
  \Var{\hat\beta \mid X} = (X^\top X)^{-1} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i^2 X_i X_i^\top\Big) (X^\top X)^{-1}
  $$

- Robust estimator: $\hat U_i^2$ in place of $\sigma_i^2$.

## $t$-ratio with robust standard errors

- Cramér convergence theorem, without proof: $Z_n \to_d Z$, $c_n \to_p c \ne 0$, $c$ non-random:
  $$
  \frac{Z_n}{c_n} \to_d \frac{Z}{c}
  $$

- $\sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj}} \to_p \sqrt{[V]_{jj}} > 0$; apply to the component CLT:
  $$
  \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} = \frac{\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j)}{\sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj}}} \to_d N(0,1)
  $$

- Asymptotic confidence interval:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  CI_{1-\alpha} = \Big[ & \hat\beta_{n,j} - z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big), \\
  & \hat\beta_{n,j} + z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)\Big]
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Coverage, $t$-ratio $\to_d Z \sim N(0, 1)$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{P}\big(\beta_j \in CI_{1-\alpha}\big) &= \mathrm{P}\Big(\Big|\frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}\Big| \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\Big) \\
  &\to \mathrm{P}\big(|Z| \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\big) \\
  &= 1 - \alpha
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Usual standard errors

- Recall:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) &= \sqrt{s^2 \big[(X^\top X)^{-1}\big]_{jj}} = \sqrt{[s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}]_{jj} / n}, \\
  s^2 &= \frac{1}{n-k} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Usual: $s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}$ estimates $\sigma^2 Q^{-1}$ under homoskedasticity.

- Robust: $\hat V_n$ estimates $V = Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}$.

## $s^2 \to_p \E{U_i^2}$

- $\E{U_i^2} < \infty$; weak LLN, consistency and Slutsky:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2 &= \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2}_{\to_p\, \E{U_i^2}} - 2\, \underbrace{(\hat\beta_n - \beta)^\top}_{\to_p\, 0^\top}\ \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i}_{\to_p\,0} \\
  &\qquad + \underbrace{(\hat\beta_n - \beta)^\top}_{\to_p\,0^\top}\ \underbrace{\Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)}_{\to_p\,Q}\ \underbrace{(\hat\beta_n - \beta)}_{\to_p\,0} \\
  &\to_p \E{U_i^2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Degrees-of-freedom correction, $k$ fixed:
  $$
  s^2 = \underbrace{\frac{n}{n-k}}_{\to\,1}\ \underbrace{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \hat U_i^2}_{\to_p\,\E{U_i^2}} \to_p \E{U_i^2}
  $$

- Homoskedasticity, law of iterated expectations:
  $$
  \E{U_i^2} = \E{\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i}} = \sigma^2
  $$

## Homoskedasticity: robust and usual agree

- Both asymptotic-variance estimators consistent:
  $$
  \hat V_n \to_p \sigma^2 Q^{-1}, \qquad s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \sigma^2 Q^{-1}
  $$

- Ratio of standard errors, $\sigma^2 [Q^{-1}]_{jj} > 0$; Slutsky:
  $$
  \frac{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} = \sqrt{\frac{[\hat V_n]_{jj}}{[s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1}]_{jj}}} \to_p 1
  $$

- Usual $t$-ratio, $A_n Z_n \to_d A Z$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} &= \underbrace{\frac{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}}_{\to_p\, 1} \cdot \underbrace{\frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)}}_{\to_d\, N(0, 1)} \\
  &\to_d N(0, 1)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Heteroskedasticity: usual standard errors fail

- Without homoskedasticity:
  $$
  s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \E{U_i^2}\, Q^{-1} \ne Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1} = V \quad \text{(in general)}
  $$

- Example, $k = 1$, no intercept: $Q = \E{X_i^2}$, $\Omega = \E{U_i^2 X_i^2}$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  V &= \frac{\E{U_i^2 X_i^2}}{\big(\E{X_i^2}\big)^2}, \qquad \text{usual: } \frac{\E{U_i^2}}{\E{X_i^2}} \\
  V - \frac{\E{U_i^2}}{\E{X_i^2}} &= \frac{\Cov{U_i^2, X_i^2}}{\big(\E{X_i^2}\big)^2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\Cov{U_i^2, X_i^2} > 0$ $\Longrightarrow$ usual standard error asymptotically too small.

## Normality: exact and asymptotic

- Normal model: $U \mid X \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n)$; under Assumptions I and II:
  $$
  \Var{\sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \mid X} = \sigma^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \sigma^2 Q^{-1}
  $$

- $\sigma^2$ estimated by $s^2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \frac{\hat\beta_{n,j} - \beta_j}{\text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)} \,\Big|\, X \sim t_{n-k} \quad \text{for every } n > k \\
  & t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2} \to z_{1-\alpha/2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Normal model: $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2$, $\E{U_i^4} = 3\sigma^4$.

- $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$ $\Longrightarrow$ robust and usual standard-error ratio $\to_p 1$.

## Usual and robust standard errors compared

- Validity of the $t$-ratio (large $n$: conditions for $\hat V_n \to_p V$):

  | Errors | Usual std. err | Robust std. err |
  |-----|----|----|
  | $U \mid X \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n)$ | exact, $t_{n-k}$ | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ |
  | $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2$ | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ |
  | $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i}$ depends on $X_i$ | invalid in general | large $n$, $N(0,1)$ |

- Homoskedasticity: standard-error ratio $\to_p 1$, $t$ quantile $\to z_{1-\alpha/2}$; asymptotically equivalent intervals:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{usual, exact (row 1):}\quad & \hat\beta_{n,j} \pm t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) \\
  \text{usual, large } n\text{:}\quad & \hat\beta_{n,j} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big) \\
  \text{robust, large } n\text{:}\quad & \hat\beta_{n,j} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}\big(\hat\beta_{n,j}\big)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Summary

## Consistency and asymptotic normality

- Assumptions for consistency $\Longrightarrow$ $\hat\beta_n \to_p \beta$.

- Normalized representation:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) = \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum X_i U_i
  $$

- Assumptions I to III:
  $$
  \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta_n - \beta) \to_d N(0, V), \qquad V = Q^{-1} \Omega Q^{-1}
  $$

- $\E{U_i^2 \mid X_i} = \sigma^2$ $\Longrightarrow$ $\Omega = \sigma^2 Q$, $V = \sigma^2 Q^{-1}$.

## Variance estimation and standard errors

- $\hat V_n = \hat Q_n^{-1} \hat\Omega_n \hat Q_n^{-1}$, $\hat Q_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum X_i X_i^\top$, $\hat\Omega_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum \hat U_i^2 X_i X_i^\top$.

- Assumptions I to III, $\E{U_i^4} < \infty$, $\E{\|X_i\|^4} < \infty$ $\Longrightarrow$ $\hat V_n \to_p V$.

- $\text{std. err}_{\text{rob}}(\hat\beta_{n,j}) = \sqrt{[\hat V_n]_{jj}/n}$; robust $t$-ratio $\to_d N(0,1)$; normal confidence interval: coverage $\to 1-\alpha$.

- Usual: $s^2 \hat Q_n^{-1} \to_p \E{U_i^2}\, Q^{-1}$; homoskedasticity: robust/usual standard-error ratio $\to_p 1$.

- Heteroskedasticity: usual standard errors invalid in general; robust valid under stated conditions.

- $U \mid X \sim N(0,\sigma^2 I_n)$: usual $t$-ratio exactly $t_{n-k}$; $t_{n-k,\,1-\alpha/2} \to z_{1-\alpha/2}$.
